# Workflows

17 ready-made graphs. Drag a `.json` onto the ComfyUI canvas, or use **Workflow → Open**.

**Every graph documents itself on its own canvas.** The MarkdownNote inside each one is the real documentation — it is the copy in front of you while you work, and everything under [`docs/`](docs/) is generated from it. Read either; they cannot disagree.

> **Calls** is how many billing nodes a run hits before you bypass anything. **Ctrl+B** on a node drops it from the run and passes its input straight through. *per input* means the node is fed a list, so it fires once for every image handed to it — a folder's worth, or a deck's, which is the difference between 3 calls and 234. *a sweep* means the Batch / Sweep node, whose count is its own grid.

## FLUX.2

Black Forest Labs endpoints, one image at a time.

| Workflow | Calls | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`flux2-batch-sweep`](flux2/flux2-batch-sweep.json) · [docs](docs/flux2-batch-sweep.md) | a sweep | Generate a whole batch from one node — variations of a single image, a folder of them, or one parameter swept across a range — without wiring up a graph per result. |
| [`flux2-structure-canny`](flux2/flux2-structure-canny.json) · [docs](docs/flux2-structure-canny.md) | 1 | Build the control map locally with Canny and hand it to FLUX.2 as an ordinary reference image, because the API itself has no control endpoint to send it to. |
| [`flux2-style-transfer`](flux2/flux2-style-transfer.json) · [docs](docs/flux2-style-transfer.md) | 1 | Two images into one FLUX.2 call: the first keeps its composition, the second lends its look, and the prompt says which is which. |
| [`flux2-variations`](flux2/flux2-variations.json) · [docs](docs/flux2-variations.md) | 4 | Four takes on one image at fixed seeds, so the set is reproducible and you can tell which seed gave you which result. |

## Stability

The control endpoints, each studied alone, chained through folders.

| Workflow | Calls | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`stability-01-sketch`](stability/stability-01-sketch.json) · [docs](docs/stability-01-sketch.md) | 3 per input | Takes an image read as line art and renders a finished picture over it. It is the endpoint for the case where the drawing is right and nothing else is. |
| [`stability-02-structure`](stability/stability-02-structure.json) · [docs](docs/stability-02-structure.md) | 3 per input | The workhorse. Takes an image read as mass, depth and arrangement and renders a new picture on that scaffolding. |
| [`stability-03-style`](stability/stability-03-style.json) · [docs](docs/stability-03-style.md) | 3 per input | Read this before you use it: this endpoint keeps none of your image's composition. |
| [`stability-04-style-transfer`](stability/stability-04-style-transfer.json) · [docs](docs/stability-04-style-transfer.md) | 3 per input | Two images in: a composition to keep and a look to apply. The only endpoint of the four with more than one dial, and the closest thing in the Stability API to what you would do locally with IPAdapter. |
| [`stability-control-routing`](stability/stability-control-routing.json) · [docs](docs/stability-control-routing.md) | 4 | The four endpoints in api.stability.ai that do ControlNet-shaped work, wired so the same image can go through any combination of them without rewiring. |

## Tarot

Deck-shaped work: whole runs, staged runs, and single-card technique studies.

| Workflow | Calls | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tarot-01-generate`](tarot/tarot-01-generate.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-01-generate.md) | 1 per input | This is the stage that costs money. It ends by writing raw, unframed art to tarot/derived-art/, one file per card, named by slot: 00_the-fool.png, 16_the-tower.png. Stage 2 picks that folder up. |
| [`tarot-02-assemble`](tarot/tarot-02-assemble.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-02-assemble.md) | free | Reads the art stage 1 wrote and turns it into finished cards. No API calls at all, so every run here is free and instant. Iterate on the border and the lettering as long as you like. |
| [`tarot-deck-derive`](tarot/tarot-deck-derive.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-deck-derive.md) | 1 per input | A seed deck in, a new deck out, in a style you locked and can lock again a year from now. |
| [`tarot-generate-and-edit`](tarot/tarot-generate-and-edit.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-generate-and-edit.md) | 5 | A chain you sit inside rather than a graph you run once. Each stage takes the previous image back in as input_image, so an edit is just another call with the last result attached. |
| [`tarot-structure-fidelity`](tarot/tarot-structure-fidelity.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-structure-fidelity.md) | 1 + a sweep | Three different dials, one card. Run them side by side and learn what each one costs you. |
| [`tarot-style-transfer`](tarot/tarot-style-transfer.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-style-transfer.md) | 2 per input | Each card keeps its own composition; one reference image lends the look to all of them. |
| [`tarot-variation-sweep`](tarot/tarot-variation-sweep.json) · [docs](docs/tarot-variation-sweep.md) | a sweep | Two sweeps off the same image, so you can see a parameter's shape instead of guessing at it. |

## What feeds what

There is no workflow-calls-a-workflow in ComfyUI. What crosses a file boundary is a folder, and these are the folders that already line up — one graph writes where another reads:

- [`tarot-01-generate`](docs/tarot-01-generate.md) → [`tarot-02-assemble`](docs/tarot-02-assemble.md)

Any other pairing works the same way: point the reader's `directory` at the writer's `output_dir`.

## Adding one

1. Drop the `.json` into the family folder it belongs to — `flux2/`, `stability/` or `tarot/`.
2. Give it a **MarkdownNote** whose first heading is its title and whose first paragraph says what it does in a sentence. That note becomes its documentation.
3. Run `python tools/workflow_docs.py`.

That is the whole process. This index and every page under `docs/` are generated by scanning the folders, so nothing has to be registered anywhere by hand — a list you have to remember to update is a list that goes stale. `python tools/workflow_docs.py --check` exits non-zero when they are behind.

Filenames keep their family prefix (`stability-01-sketch.json`, not `01-sketch.json`) because ComfyUI shows the bare filename in its tab, and with several graphs open the prefix is the only thing telling them apart.

---

17 graphs. Running every fixed-cost one once comes to 16 calls; the *per input* and *sweep* graphs are on top of that and depend on what you feed them.
